lane: Mobile: fixes from the Android device test of 28/11/2026 (book art, onboarding gate, chat room header and suggestions, daily line, hub filter)
goal: Close the five findings the Owner picked from the 28/11 device test: own art for Kinh Pháp Cú and Kinh Dịch, no second onboarding for an account that already finished it, a readable chat-room header and suggestions that leave once used, one daily line drawn from the whole library instead of one per book (with copy that no longer says 'five books'), and a hub filter that survives a tab switch.
successCriteria: Kinh Pháp Cú and Kinh Dịch show their own cover and thumbnail (reviewed, no text, no figure), the borrowed-art tint is gone, and validate:visual-assets passes.

A signed-in account whose server profile says onboarding is complete never sees the 'BƯỚC 2/2' onboarding again, even when the local profile is missing or still says not onboarded; the decision lives in a pure, unit-tested function.

The chat room header shows the guide name in full (up to two lines) with a short subtitle; quick replies the reader already sent disappear, the rest wrap instead of being cut at the right edge, and none show while a reply is being written.

'Một câu cho hôm nay' becomes one line a day drawn from the whole library (stable for the day, same line on Home and on the screen); the screen has no per-book tabs or 'other books today' list; Explore no longer says 'năm cuốn sách xưa'; the title is replaced with more refined copy.
The Trò chuyện hub keeps the chosen filter (for example 'Sách') after the reader switches tab or opens a guide and comes back, until the app is closed.
tsc, mobile jest, validate:data, admin:check and validate:visual-assets pass.
untouchedSurfaces: supabase/** is not edited: profile-upsert and the profile snapshot read stay as they are; no SQL, no deploy.
packages/agent-config/feature-access.json and apps/admin/feature-access.js keep the internal label 'Một câu cho hôm nay' because the spec is mirrored in a SQL migration; only app-facing copy changes.
Book quote content files (packages/content/data/book-quotes/*.json, Owner-approved 27/11) are read, not edited.
No dependency, no secret, .env not read, no account created.

impact.entryPoint: App start (profile restore), Trò chuyện hub and chat room, Home card and Explore row for the daily line, a book guide's detail page.
impact.dataWrite: No new data shape. Restoring a profile may now take onboarded=true from the account's own server snapshot and save it locally, which is the value the server already holds.
impact.backendContract: Unchanged. The app reads the existing profile snapshot more often (when the local profile is missing or not onboarded), with the same request.
impact.adminVisibility: Only the App.tsx digest in apps/admin/workflow-catalog.js is refreshed.
impact.privacySafety: No new personal data is shown or sent. The profile snapshot is the signed-in user's own row. New art has no people or religious figures.
impact.observability: Existing book_quote events keep their names; the opened event now reports the book of the line shown.
impact.rollback: Revert the commit; the screens and restore logic return to the previous behaviour with no data migration.

canonicalContracts: docs/BRAND_GUIDELINES.md (48 px touch target, support large text and wrapping, the right portrait for each guide)

managerTestPath: Install the new build over the old one with an account that finished onboarding: it opens on Home, not on BƯỚC 2/2. Open Trò chuyện, tap Sách, go to Home and back: Sách is still selected; Kinh Pháp Cú and Kinh Dịch have their own pictures. Open Kinh Dịch and chat: the header shows the full guide name; a suggestion you tapped is gone and the rest wrap. On Home, the daily line card and the screen it opens show the same single line; Explore no longer mentions five books.
residualRisk: All fixes are verified in unit tests only until a new Android build is installed. The exact cause of the device's second onboarding was not reproduced; the fix covers the two paths that can cause it (local profile not onboarded, or missing with a failed server read).
